title: Florence Nightingale's birth chart
metaDescription: Florence Nightingale's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.6° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 22.7° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 21.6° Taurus. That falls in the third decan, 20°–30°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — an earth sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 25.7° Aries, Venus was at 6.7° Cancer, Mars was at 10.5° Leo. Read together: a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Uranus square Pluto, 0.1° of separation. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable. Behind it, Mars trine Saturn at 1.2°, and Neptune square Pluto at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Taurus at 22.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Pisces at 17.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Aries at 9.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in fire, 3 in earth, 3 in water by element, 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 3 mutable by modality. A fire-weighted chart runs hot at the start line — initiative is its native language. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus and Neptune were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.8° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 22.7°.
